mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, which in turn results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in real estate sales (HOUST) signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which boosts corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) over a 3-month period, it indicates strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > CPIAUCSL growth over 3 months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between relative RSAFS growth and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 over a month, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is negative, it indicates a recessionary environment with accommodative monetary policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate prolonged economic weakness.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between the interaction of low FEDFUNDS and negative GDP growth with negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between HOUST increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
